speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned persistent bleeding after your wisdom tooth extraction and a history of easy bruising; to start, have you experienced any spontaneous bleeding, such as nosebleeds or bleeding gums, prior to the extraction?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Given your uncle's history of joint swelling and bleeding, could you describe any specific joint pain or swelling you have experienced? Also, does the bleeding from your gums stop completely, or does it only slow down with pressure?

REQUEST TEST: PT/PTT (Prothrombin Time/Partial Thromboplastin Time)

speaker: Doctor
text: The results show your PT is normal, but your PTT is prolonged at 60 seconds, which suggests a problem with the intrinsic clotting pathway. Given your family history of joint swelling and bleeding, have you ever experienced swelling in your joints without an injury?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged PTT and family history of joint swelling are highly suggestive of Hemophilia A or B; have you noticed bleeding into your joints during sports or minor falls? REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII Activity Level. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Knee to check for hemarthrosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A (Factor VIII deficiency). The prolonged PTT combined with a critically low Factor VIII activity level (12%) and your family history of joint swelling confirms this diagnosis. I will be placing a diagnosis now.
